outcome: health service costs associated with labor induction
cohort: 412 women admitted for induction of labor at a tertiary hospital in Spain
finding: Cesarean delivery, a very unfavorable cervix (Bishop score <2), and labor induction for hypertensive disorders of pregnancy were associated with higher costs following induction of labor.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery after labor induction was significantly more expensive than spontaneous delivery and instrumental vaginal delivery.
